novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism and measurement in emergent-misalignment fine-tuning: risk is predicted by "how strongly the dataset's activations already project onto the pre-existing linear misalignment direction" together with "the cosine coupling between the low-rank update the dataset would induce and that misalignment direction." Searches using "emergent misalignment prediction before fine-tuning gradient alignment," "base-model geometry task gradient misalignment direction," and "precondition model against harmful fine-tuning" found the closest precedents in Navigating the Safety Landscape/VISAGE, Representation Noising, and In-Training Defenses against Emergent Misalignment; these respectively probe a model-level safety basin or defend against harmful fine-tuning, but do not provide the claimed dataset-specific, zero-step coupling predictor. The step is a substantive natural extension combining established linear safety directions, single-gradient estimates, and pre-fine-tuning defenses rather than a wholly new paradigm; the particular predictive relationship is apparently new, while the one-time "Pre-Conditioning" defense has substantial conceptual precedent in Representation Noising and related tamper-resistant alignment work.
